expectations.text: The bottom line clearly AGREES that adding a unique constraint/index on email is the right move (a plain yes, possibly with caveats), rather than rejecting or hedging it.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Council verdict: Yes, with changes." and "Adding a unique index is the right fix. Put it on the normalised email, not the raw column." Option 3 marked "recommended", blind vote 3-0. | grader 2: "Council verdict: Yes, with changes." and "Adding a unique index is the right fix."

expectations.text: Addresses case-insensitive uniqueness (e.g. a unique index on lower(email), or citext).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "A plain unique index on the raw email column still lets case variants through." Recommends normalising to lower(btrim(email)) with a CHECK constraint, or "an expression index on (lower(btrim(email)))"; cites the citext docs. | grader 2: "Put it on the normalised email, not the raw column"; "Under the default collation a plain unique index compares case-sensitively... the PostgreSQL citext docs say such an index won't enforce uniqueness case-insensitively"

expectations.text: Says existing duplicate rows must be found and resolved before the unique index can be built.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: Step 1 gives the duplicate-detection query; step 3 "Merge the existing duplicates"; "it fails and leaves an INVALID index if duplicates exist or arrive during the build, so removing duplicates first is part of the fix." | grader 2: "3. Merge the existing duplicates..." and "removing duplicates first is part of the fix"; also diagnostic query for duplicates in step 1

expectations.text: Recommends building the index without blocking writes (e.g. CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) or otherwise addresses locking on a ~4M-row table.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY users_email_uq ON users (email)", "Run it outside any transaction... with SET lock_timeout='5s'", "Never drop CONCURRENTLY to make the migration pass: without it the build blocks writes to users for its whole duration." | grader 2: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY users_email_uq ON users (email)" and "Never drop CONCURRENTLY to make the migration pass: without it the build blocks writes to users for its whole duration."

expectations.text: Mentions handling the unique-violation error / race at signup in the application.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "At signup, catch SQLSTATE 23505 and return the same neutral message as a normal signup... Never sign the user in on a conflict. Map 23505 in email-change, admin and import paths too" plus the check-then-insert race explanation. | grader 2: "7. At signup, catch SQLSTATE 23505 and return the same neutral message as a normal signup... Never sign the user in on a conflict."

expectations.text: Does not manufacture a blocking objection to the core proposal.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: The caveats (normalisation, root cause of the two bugs, tenant scoping) are framed as refinements, not blockers: "Yes, with changes", "Adding a unique index is the right fix." The root-cause caveat is a genuine, non-blocking risk rather than an invented objection. | grader 2: The response endorses the index throughout ("Adding a unique index is the right fix", option 3 marked ✅ recommended) and only raises scoped caveats (root-cause uncertainty, tenant scoping) rather than rejecting or gatekeeping the core proposal.
